body.p: The following remarks are made in response to the Action. In this response, claims 1, 4, and 10 have been amended. Claim 7 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. No claims have been newly added. Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 are pending. The claim amendments are supported by at least, for example, paragraphs [0042]-[0044], [0047], and [0048] of the Specification as filed. There is no new matter.
The drawings are objected to under 37 CFR §1.83(a) for failing to show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Applicant traverses the objection.

Without agreeing to the correctness of the objection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 7 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. The objection is moot. Applicant requests withdrawal of the objection.
Claim Rejection - 35 USC % 112
Claim 7 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) as failing to comply with the written description requirement. Applicant traverses the rejection.

Without agreeing to the correctness of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 7 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. The rejection is moot. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.
Claims 1-4 and 6-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Applicant traverses the rejection.
Without agreeing to the propriety of the objection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to recite, in part:
a hollow shaft extending along a first axis thereof and coupled to the first arm
link;
a first stage reduction assembly extending along a second axis thereof and
coupled to a power source of the robot; and
a second stage reduction assembly comprising:
an input of the second stage reduction assembly coupled to an output of the
first stage reduction assembly,
wherein the input of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to rotate
about the second axis; and
an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a
periphery of the hollow shaft,
wherein the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a
rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft about the first axis;
wherein the first axis is offset from the second axis in a direction of the second
stage reduction assembly.
For at least the following reasons, the claims are definite.

A person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) would be able to appreciate the subject matter being claimed from the above recited features of amended claim 1. The "first axis" is the axis of the "hollow shaft," and the "second axis" is the axis of the "first stage reduction assembly." A POSITA would appreciate that the "first axis [being] offset from the second axis in a direction of the second stage reduction assembly," is then a function of the respective locations of the "input" and the "output" in the direction of the "second stage reduction assembly." It would be clear to a POSITA that the "offset" between the "first axis" and the "second axis" is therefore a fixed distance in the direction of the "second stage reduction assembly." Therefore, a POSITA would not interpret the "offset," as recited in claim 1 to be the offset angle between the respective axes. Thus, claims 1-4 and 6-10 are definite. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.
Claims 1, 2, and 7-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by CN 107284541 ("Wang"). Applicant traverses this rejection.

Without agreeing to the correctness of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to recite, in part, "a second stage reduction assembly comprising: an input of the second stage reduction assembly coupled to an output of the first stage reduction assembly, ... and an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft," and "wherein the second stage reduction assembly further comprises a belt connected to the input of the second stage reduction assembly and the output of the second stage reduction assembly and via which
the input of the second stage reduction assembly and the output of the second stage reduction assembly engage with each other."

The Action states that Wang discloses the "second stage reduction assembly (13, 12, 9, 10, 17, 18, 8, 11) comprising: an input (13) ... coupled to an output (output shaft of 14) of the first stage reduction assembly, ... to rotate about a second axis (axis of 13) ... and an output (9, 10, 17, 18, 8, 11) ... coaxially arranged on a periphery (periphery of 6 receiving 9/10/17/18/8/11 thereon)." (Action at p. 5.) The Action also states that Wang discloses the "second stage reduction assembly further comprises a belt (17 and/or 18) via which the input of the second stage reduction assembly and the output of the second stage reduction assembly engage with each other." (Action at p. 5.) For at least the following reasons, Wang does not disclose the above recited feature of amended claim
Wang discloses the "output shaft of star decelerator 14 is connected with the drive bevel gear 13." (Wang at p. 2, 9th paragraph of machine translation.) Wang also discloses:

First driving wheel 9 is connected with first driven pulley 8 with the first crawler belt 17, first driving wheel 9, described First driven pulley 8 and first crawler belt 17 constitute the first caterpillar wheel group; Second driving wheel 10 and described second driven Wheel 11 is connected with the second crawler belt 18, and second driving wheel 10, second driven pulley 11 and second
crawler belt 18 constitute the Two caterpillar wheel groups.

(Wang at p. 2, 10th paragraph of machine translation.) Wang does not disclose the "second stage reduction assembly, " as recited in amended claim 1. Assuming that the "first driven pulley 8," the "first driving wheel 9," the "second driving wheel 10," the "second driven wheel 11," the "first crawler belt 17," and the "second crawler belt 18," in Wang discloses the "output," as recited in amended claim 1 (which it does not), the "planetary reduction gear 13," and the components of the "output," in Wang do not disclose the "second stage reduction assembly," as recited in claim 1. In Wang, the "hollow shaft 6" is located between and mechanically couples the "planetary reduction gear 13," to the components of the "output" (i.e., 9, 10, 17, 18, 8, and 11). Therefore, either the
"second stage reduction assembly" in Wang discloses including the "hollow shaft 6" or Wang discloses a second and third stage reduction assembly. However, Wang does not

disclose the "second stage reduction assembly compris[es] an input of the second stage reduction assembly coupled to an output of the first stage reduction assembly, ... and an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft," as recited in amended claim 1.

Moreover, Wang does not disclose the "first crawler belt 17," or the "second crawler belt 18," is connected to the "planetary reduction gear 13," and the components of the "output," (i.e., 9, 10, 17, 18, 8, and 11) and via which the "planetary reduction gear 13," and the "output," engage with each other as recited in amended claim 1. In Wang, the "first crawler belt 17," is connected to the "first driven pulley 8" and the "first driving wheel 9," and the "second crawler belt 18" is connected to the "second driving wheel 10" and the "second driven wheel 11." Therefore, Wang does not disclose that the either the "first crawler belt 17," or the "second crawler belt 18" connect to or engage with the "planetary reduction gear 13," as recited in claim 1. Instead, Wang discloses the "first driving wheel 9 and second master driving wheel 10 is sequentially connected installed in the other end of the hollow shaft 6, first driving wheel 9 and second driving wheel 10 synchronous axial systems." (Wang at p. 2, 9th paragraph of machine translation.) Therefore, in Wang, it appears that the "driven wheel of differential 12" and the "hollow shaft 6" discloses connecting the "planetary reduction gear 13" to the components of the "output," and it is via the "driven wheel of differential 12" and the "hollow shaft 6" that the "planetary reduction gear 13" and the components of the "output" engage with each other. Therefore, Wang does not disclose "wherein the second stage reduction assembly further comprises a belt via which the input of the second stage reduction assembly and the output of the second stage reduction assembly engage with each other," as recited in claim 1. Thus, Wang fails to disclose each and every feature of amended claim 1.

Furthermore, the Action does not provide any support for its characterization that Wang teaches "second stage reduction assembly," as recited in claim 1. Instead, the Action relies on the drawings of Wang to make conclusory assertions of the configuration of the components and their corresponding function based on the figures.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2 and 7-9 are not anticipated by Wang. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness
of the rejection with respect to features not discussed. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.
Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by CN 208645329 ("Pei"). Applicant traverses this rejection.

Claim 1 recites, in part, "a first arm link." The Action states that Pei discloses the "first arm link 48." (Action at . 6.) For at least the following reasons, Pei does not disclose the above recited feature of claim 1.

Pei discloses the "splined shaft 43 is hollow shaft, and top connects equipped with rotary pneumatic [f]irst 48." (Pei at p. 3, 20th paragraph of machine translation). In Pei, the "rotary pneumatic first 48" does not disclose the "first arm link," as recited in claim 1. Instead, Pei discloses that the "structure of four articulated robot ... as shown in Figure 1 to Figure 8, including hanger 10, a first cantilever 20, a second cantilever 30, the first cantilever drive device, the second cantilever drive device and a hand driving device." (Pei at p. 3, 13th paragraph of machine translation.) In Pei, and as shown in FIG. 2, the "first cantilever 20," and the "second cantilever 30," disclose being arm links of the "four-joint robot structure." Therefore, Pei does not disclose the "rotary pneumatic first 48," is an "arm link," as recited in claim 1. Instead, it appears that Pei discloses the "rotary pneumatic first 48" is a pneumatic connector rather than an "arm link" of the robot. Thus, Pei does not disclose the "first arm link" as recited in claim 1.

Amended claim 1 recites, in part, "an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft, wherein the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft about the first axis." The Action states that Pei discloses the "output (47) of the second stage reduction assembly [and] the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted (via belt 46) to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft." (Action at p. 6.) The Action also states that Pei discloses the "elements 48 and 43 are shown to be connected to rotate together within a common upper bearing." (Action at p. 9.) For at least the following reasons, Pei does not disclose the above recited features of amended claim 1.

Pei discloses the "[t]hird tooth belt driver includes driving pulley 45, ... and passive belt wheel 47, driving pulley 45 are fixed on the output shaft of the planet-gear speed reducer 42, and passive belt wheel 47 is fixed on spline housing 44." (Pei at p. 3, 21st paragraph of machine translation.) Pei also discloses:

The rotating mechanism 40 includes rotating electric machine 41, planet- gear reducer 42, third tooth belt driver, splined shaft 43 [w]ith spline housing 44. Spline housing 44 is mounted on before the second cantilever 30 in the bearing bore of end bearing block 31 by bearing 32, and splined shaft 43 is worn [through t]he splined hole of spline housing 44.... The upper end of
splined shaft 43 is connect[ed] with hoisting mechanism 50.

(Pei at p. 3, 20th paragraph of machine translation.) Pei does not disclose the "passive belt wheel 47" is adapted to cause a rotation of the "rotary pneumatic first 48" via the "splined shaft 43" and "spline housing 44," as recited in claim 1. Instead, Pei discloses the "passive belt wheel 47 is fixed on spline housing 44." Therefore, although the "rotary pneumatic first 48," in Pei may be rotatable, Pei does not disclose the "passive belt wheel 47" is adapted to cause a rotation of the "rotary pneumatic first 48" via the "splined shaft 43" and "spline housing 44," as recited in amended claim 1.

Moreover, in Pei, the "spline housing 44 is mounted on before the second cantilever 30 in the bearing bore of end bearing block 31 by bearing 32." In Pei, the "spline housing 44" is arranged in the "end bearing block 31," and by "bearing 32," to allow the "second cantilever 30" to rotate about the axis of the "splined shaft 43," to provide the "four-joint robot structure." Pei does not disclose the "passive belt wheel 47," the "splined shaft 43," or the "spline housing 44," causes rotation of the "rotary pneumatic first 48." The Action does not provide any support for its characterization that the "passive belt wheel 47" in Pei is adapted to cause a rotation of the "rotary pneumatic first 48" via the "splined shaft 43" and "spline housing 44," as in amended claim 1. Instead, the Action relies only on the drawings of Pei, which do not disclose any such rotation caused by the "passive belt wheel 47," the "splined shaft 43," or the "spline housing 44," to make conclusory assertions of how the components function based on the figures. Therefore, Pei does not disclose "an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft, wherein the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the second stage reduction
assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft about the first axis," as recited in amended claim 1.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2- 4, 6, 8, and 9 are not anticipated by Pei. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness of the rejection with respect to features not discussed. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.

It is submitted that the rejections in the Action have been successfully traversed and that the application is now in condition for allowance. Reconsideration of the application and allowance thereof is solicited.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific allegation or comment of the Action does not signify agreement or concession with that part. Also, the arguments herein are not exhaustive. The amendment or cancelation of a claim or other part of the Specification does not necessarily signify concession with an allegation or comment of the Action. Applicant reserves the right to prosecute the rejected claims in further prosecution of this or related applications.
Authorization is hereby provided to charge any fees which may be required for the present filing, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 501561.
